title: ApplicationSet CRD was written with client-side apply — the 3.3 upgrade fails on the annotation size limit

detection.reason: the agent projects whether the CRD carries a kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration annotation (as a boolean — never the annotation itself, which is a copy of the ~1.4MB schema)

quote: In this version, the ApplicationSet CRD exceeds the size limit for client-side apply, meaning that the previous upgrade methods will result in `The CustomResourceDefinition "applicationsets.argoproj.io" is invalid: metadata.annotations: Too long: may not be more than 262144 bytes`
remediation: Re-apply the Argo CD manifests with Server-Side Apply before or as part of the 3.3 upgrade: `kubectl apply -n argocd --server-side --force-conflicts -f manifests/install.yaml`, or `ServerSideApply=true` in the syncOptions of the Application that manages Argo CD itself. A Helm install is not affected. Absence of this finding is not proof of Server-Side Apply — a Helm-managed CRD sets neither marker. If you set `ClientSideApplyMigration=false` as a workaround on 3.3.0/3.3.1, remove it after 3.3.2.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd applicationsets.argoproj.io --show-managed-fields -o json | jq -r '(.metadata.annotations["kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration"] != null | tostring) + " " + ([(.metadata.managedFields // [])[].manager] | unique | join(","))' # true, or kubectl-client-side-apply among the managers = client-side applied; upgrade with --server-side --force-conflicts

title: Source Hydrator stops committing on every DRY commit — hydration state moves to git notes

detection.reason: whether any automation depends on a hydrated commit per DRY commit lives outside the cluster; the hint names the Applications that use the Source Hydrator

quote: **Starting with v3.3, the Source Hydrator uses git notes to record the state of the most recently hydrated DRY commit instead of creating a hydrated commit on every DRY commit.**
remediation: Update automation that used hydrated commits as a signal to consult the git note in the Source Hydrator namespace instead; no action otherwise.
verifyCommand: kubectl get applications -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.sourceHydrator != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # Applications printed use the Source Hydrator

title: Source Hydrator no longer deletes stale files in the application path

detection.reason: whether a hydration path accumulates files nobody else cleans up is a repository fact; the hint names the Applications that use the Source Hydrator

quote: Starting with v3.3, this cleaning logic has been removed. The hydrator will now only overwrite or create files that correspond to the current manifest output; any additional files or obsolete data in the application path will remain untouched unless explicitly overwritten.
remediation: If your workflow relied on the hydrator wiping the path (renamed or removed manifests), add your own cleanup step for the hydrated paths of the Applications named here.
verifyCommand: kubectl get applications -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.sourceHydrator != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " -> " + (.spec.sourceHydrator.syncSource.path // "")' # paths printed no longer get cleaned before each hydration

title: Cluster version label switches to `vMajor.Minor.Patch` in 3.3.3 — cluster generators on the old form match nothing

detection.reason: the agent projects every value an ApplicationSet's cluster generators select on the argocd.argoproj.io/kubernetes-version label (matrix/merge nesting included); a bare Major.Minor value is the pre-change form. Evaluated only when the gate finds a cluster Secret carrying auto-label-cluster-info — the condition upstream states

gate.reason: upstream conditions the breakage on cluster Secrets that carry argocd.argoproj.io/auto-label-cluster-info — only those have their kubernetes-version label rewritten to vMajor.Minor.Patch; a label you maintain by hand keeps matching

quote: Application Sets with Cluster Generators, that fetch clusters based on their Kubernetes version and use `argocd.argoproj.io/auto-label-cluster-info` on the cluster secret, need to be updated to use `argocd.argoproj.io/kubernetes-version` with the `vMajor.Minor.Patch` format instead of the previous `Major.Minor` format.
remediation: These ApplicationSets select on the old `Major.Minor` form and at least one cluster Secret carries `argocd.argoproj.io/auto-label-cluster-info`, so the label they match is rewritten to `vMajor.Minor.Patch` at this version: change the selector values (for example `v1.32.13` instead of `1.32`) before upgrading. The breakage is SILENT: the generator matches no cluster and its Applications disappear without an error or an event.
verifyCommand: kubectl get applicationsets -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.. | ."argocd.argoproj.io/kubernetes-version"? // empty | tostring] | map(test("^v[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+$") | not) | any) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # names printed still select on the old Major.Minor format, which matches no cluster after the change

title: `ARGOCD_K8S_TCP_TIMEOUT` no longer sets the Kubernetes server-side timeout

detection.reason: container environment variable names are not part of the projection; the hint names the Argo CD workloads whose env would carry ARGOCD_K8S_TCP_TIMEOUT

quote: From now onwards, the Kubernetes server-side timeout is controlled by a separate environment variable.
remediation: If you tuned `ARGOCD_K8S_TCP_TIMEOUT` to lengthen slow API-server requests, set `ARGOCD_K8S_SERVER_SIDE_TIMEOUT` as well — the old variable now only governs the TCP timeout.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get deploy,sts -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[].env[]?.name == "ARGOCD_K8S_TCP_TIMEOUT") | .kind + " " + .metadata.name' # workloads printed set the TCP timeout — add ARGOCD_K8S_SERVER_SIDE_TIMEOUT if the server-side timeout was the point

title: `--self-heal-backoff-cooldown-seconds` on the application controller is deprecated

detection.reason: checked in the application controller's container args only — the same setting made through argocd-cmd-params-cm is a ConfigMap VALUE and is not scanned

quote: The `--self-heal-backoff-cooldown-seconds` flag of the `argocd-application-controller` has been deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
remediation: Drop the flag from the controller's args (and the matching `controller.self.heal.backoff.cooldown.seconds` parameter) before a later release removes it and the controller refuses to start.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get sts,deploy -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].args[]?] | any(test("self-heal-backoff-cooldown-seconds"))) | .kind + " " + .metadata.name' # workloads printed still pass the deprecated flag

title: Bundled Kustomize 5.8.1: exec-plugin argument parsing and Helm namespace propagation change

detection.reason: which Applications render through Kustomize exec plugins or Helm charts inside kustomizations lives in Git, not in the inventory

quote: However, note that Kustomize 5.7.1 introduces code to replace the `shlex` library used for parsing arguments in exec plugins. If any existing manifests become corrupted, please follow the instructions in the 5.7.1 release notes.
remediation: Render kustomizations that use exec plugins or Helm charts with Kustomize 5.8.x before upgrading; argument quoting for exec plugins and namespace propagation into Helm charts both changed.
